column1: # The name-reference census of the deploy-channel trio (WEBHOOK_DEPLOY_SECRET, CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID,
# CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET and every name in their token family: *_NEXT, TF_VAR_ and lower-case spellings),
# a REGRESSION RATCHET, not a reachability proof. Every (file, name) key that names the family in code has a
# row here; the file only ratchets forward (see the suite header for the exact rules):
#   - a key absent from the merge-base copy is RED unless an @allow line for that exact (file, name) exists
#     at the merge-base and the same diff deletes it (land a reviewed @allow-only PR first); a NEW @allow line
#     is itself admitted only in a baseline/ADR-241-only diff whose ADR diff adds
#   - the tag of a key never changes and equals the group computed from its path; its class only moves
#     tier-a -> tier-b|sink, except sink -> tier-a (a read shape appeared in a sink file), which needs an ADR-241 line
#     'Reclass: <file> <NAME> ... Ruled by <owner>' for each moved key in a diff that touches only this baseline,
#     ADR-241 and the moved key's own file (tier-b -> tier-a has no lane); its expiry is never later (a re-date needs
#     an ADR-241 line 'Re-date: <YYYY-MM-DD> ... Ruled by <owner>' in a baseline/ADR-only diff);
#   - a row whose consumer no longer names the family is RED (the PR that moves a consumer deletes its row), and
#     so is a deleted row whose name reappears as a KEY (a read shape, or a file outside the exempt class) of a file
#     ADDED by the same diff, unless that key spends a reserved @allow; a file in the exempt class that merely
#     MENTIONS the name has no key and is not a consumer;
#   - the base copy FAILS CLOSED: an unresolved ref or any failing git call is RED (TRIO_ALLOW_NO_BASE=1 is a
# 'Ruled by' lines are self-attested text in this repository: the ratchet defends against accident and drift, not
# against a PR author (the platform does not require a second reviewer).
# Records (tab-separated; '#' lines and blank lines are ignored):
#   @stems / @exempt / @binary / @kbcode   the pinned guard constants (stems of the name family; the structural
#                                          test class: directory segments ; suffixes; the binary extensions that are
#                                          skipped; the code extensions ; basenames that ARE scanned under knowledge-base/ and
#                                          docs/, where any file starting with a shebang is code too). Each must equal the
#                                          scanner constant AND the base copy's record.
#   @allow file name max-expiry tag        a reserved NEW key (not a row; T1 does not require a row until the consumer
#                                          exists); its tag is the group computed from file
#   file name class expires tag            a row
# Classes (COMPUTED by the scanner; the baseline must agree, T5c):
#   tier-a  a READ SHAPE in a file that names the trio: any `doppler run` or `doppler secrets get|download`
#           COMMAND (regardless of arguments; only option flags may sit between `doppler` and the subcommand, prose
#           that merely contains the words is not one), ${{ secrets.<NAME> }}, a ${!var} indirection of a family name,
#           terraform output -raw access_service_token_client_*; or a workflow naming the trio in a job without a
#           literal Tier-B environment (an expression, a matrix, unparseable YAML are not literals); or a composite
#           action; any FALLBACK:* or ALIAS:* row. Expiry required (strict ISO, at most MAX_EXPIRY 2027-03-31).
#           TERMINAL: the end state is ZERO tier-a rows.
#   tier-b  a workflow with no read shape where every job naming the trio (every job, when a workflow-level key
#           names it) declares a literal environment: in the Tier-B set (single-sourced from the sibling Tier-B
#   sink    a non-workflow file with no read shape (variables.tf, server.tf, hooks.json.tmpl, host scripts). Expiry '-'.
# Tags: #9294:PR-n is the consumer group of the plan, COMPUTED from the path by the scanner (a row or @allow whose
# tag differs is RED). ALIAS:ACCESS_SERVICE_TOKEN_CLIENT_ID|SECRET rows cover the Terraform spellings of the DEPLOY
# Access token (tunnel.tf) and `terraform output -raw`; the ci_ssh and registry_push tokens are other credentials (G1b).
# FALLBACK:<NAME> rows record `|| doppler secrets get <other credential>` on a (continuation-joined) line that names the
# trio. The :- and `|| echo` fallback shapes wait for PR-2.
# EXPIRY 2026-11-30 (tier-a rows). The git-data plaintext-volume date is 2026-11-12 and the plan sequences G1 behind
# the git-data rehearsal and wipe (Ruled by CTO agent, 2026-10-15, D-1): PR-2 to PR-4 either finish before the
# rehearsal dispatch or resume after the wipe, so every row must outlive the wipe window and force the move soon
# after it. Past expiry is a hard RED only on a blocking event that touches a tier-a row's file, this baseline or
# ADR-241; on a main push, schedule, merge-queue gate or dispatch-on-main it is a non-blocking annotation (T3m), so an
# expired row never stops a tenant deploy. Within 21 days: a T3w warning.
# KNOWN BLIND SPOTS (this census names; it does not trace). Reach WITHOUT naming is closed by deleting the Tier-A
# and repo-secret copies and by the main-only environment policy (sibling census G1b-G1d, G1h), not here:
#   - `doppler run -c prd_terraform` injecting the whole project, and bulk `doppler secrets download`, in a file that
#     does not itself name the trio;
#   - `secrets: inherit` and `toJSON(secrets)` into a callee workflow, and loader adoption (a job that uses the infra
#     credentials loader without naming a trio name);
#   - computed names (`secrets[format(...)]`, `"${n}_DEPLOY_SECRET"`), and a ${!var} indirection whose family name is
#   - callers of a baselined script that fetches the trio itself (infra-config-verify.sh, verify-tunnel-ingress-origin.sh);
# Acceptance criterion 1 is therefore: zero tier-a rows PLUS the owner-run deletion postcondition in the final PR body.
# The G1b names (CI_SSH_ACCESS_TOKEN_*, DEPLOY_SSH_PRIVATE_KEY) are not tracked here (separate property, #8609).
# REGENERATE (derived from the tree, never hand-listed): keep this prose header and replace everything below it with
# (it prints the pinned records, the @allow lines that have not been spent, and the rows; an existing key keeps its tag
# and its possibly re-dated expiry, a key that spends an @allow takes the allow's tag and max-expiry, a new key takes the
# group tag and expiry 2026-11-30 on tier-a).
